title: The relay cannot escape the cone
promptMarkdown: Prove that the sum of two future-directed causal displacements is future-directed causal. Give necessary and sufficient conditions for a nonzero sum to be null. As a check, a light ray travels from $(ct,x,y)=(0,0,0)$ to $(3,3,0)\,\mathrm m$, is redirected, and arrives at $(7,3,4)\,\mathrm m$. Classify the endpoint separation and explain why the ray's own path has zero proper time although the endpoint separation is timelike.
hintLadder: Use the ordinary spatial triangle inequality, then the causal bound.
Inspect equality in both inequalities, allowing a zero vector.
Compare the integral along a path with the interval of its endpoints.
